title: intent upgrade destroys every issue in an already-migrated v3 project
body:
Silent, total, and the output actively reassures.

REPRODUCED, two arms, both v3 binaries, in a throwaway project:

    v3 release (dirty-69f672d3)   issues 5 -> 0   threads intact
    v3 debug   (dirty-ad0ba20d)   issues 5 -> 0   threads intact
    v2 2.19.0, REAL 2.10.0 -> 2.19.0 migration    issues 5 -> 5   CLEAN

v3-ONLY. Under hv's freeze scope this is a v3-only fix and does not land in
Intentv2. The first v2 arm was a FALSE CLEAN -- v2 printed "already at 2.19.0"
and short-circuited, so it measured only that a no-op destroys nothing. The
declared version was backdated to 2.10.0 to force a real migration.

THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS IS THAT ASYMMETRY. v2's upgrade SHORT-CIRCUITS at target.
v3's does NOT: on an already-migrated project it prints "already migrated: N
thread(s) had committed canon and were re-emitted from it rather than converted"
and re-runs the migration. Threads survive that re-run; issues do not.

THE OUTPUT IS THE WORST PART, AND IT IS THE SAME LINE IN BOTH:
    live   "migrated: 58 thread(s), 0 issue(s), 95 file(s)"
    probe  "migrated: 1 thread(s), 0 issue(s), 6 file(s) written"
The probe held FIVE, reported ZERO, and left ZERO. So "0 issue(s)" means it LEFT
none, not that it FOUND none.

HOW IT REACHED THIS REPO: dc's `int hosting --include-mutating` did not contain
its mutators (fixed; containment now proven by fingerprint plus positive
control), so `upgrade` ran against the live project at 2026-08-24 13:44:15Z and
emptied 47 issues. The escape is how it arrived; the bug is in the verb and would
have reached the repo eventually through the front door.

REGRESSION TEST WARNING (cc): a test that asserts via `sync`'s agreement report
INHERITS intent#0069. Assert on counts read from the store directly, never on
sync reporting AGREE -- otherwise the reporting defect hides this one's
regression. The repro script asserts on counts, which is why it can see the loss.

Repro: upgrade_issue_loss.sh, two arms, self-contained under mktemp.

RESOLVED 2026-08-24 17:37Z. Fix by cc at `3f367cf8`; filed, reproduced and
bounded by dc, and closed by dc so the finder and the fixer stay separate on
the record.

THE FIX: `migrate::plan` now unions `issues` against committed canon, mirroring
`dehydrated()`. `orphaned_issues()` sits beside it, and the strict single-issue
reader was extracted as `ingest::read_issue` so there is ONE reader rather than
a second one inlined at the call site.

AND THE REPORT WAS FIXED WITH IT, WHICH THIS BODY ASKED FOR. The union counts
issues read back from canon, so `migrated: N issue(s)` would have claimed as
CONVERTED what it merely re-emitted. `Plan` and `Upgraded` now carry
`already_migrated_issues` and print it on its own line. Leaving the output
asymmetric would have rebuilt this issue's own shape one layer up.

NO THIRD INSTANCE, AND IT IS ENUMERATED RATHER THAN REASONED. `store.rs:1591`
deletes SEVEN tables. Five are Thread sub-populations and return with the
threads; of the two top-level members, `threads` already had its union, so
`issues` was the only one without. Confirmed independently by dc from
`sqlite_master` on the live store rather than from a second reading of the
source: 17 tables, 5 of them FTS5 shadows of `doc_sections`, 12 logical, and
12 minus 7 is 5.

GREEN ON THIS ISSUE'S OWN REPRO WITH THE POSITIVE CONTROL FREE: the fixed debug
build reads 5 -> 5 while the still-pre-fix release binary reads 5 -> 0 in the
SAME run, so the green is a property of the fix and not of the instrument going
blind. Both arms were needed for that and one would not have given it.
